title: Peg In Hole
summary: The hovering aerial manipulator starts holding a metal peg (a cylinder 15 cm long and 4 cm in diameter) in its gripper, pointing straight ahead. A wall stands ahead with a blue square socket mounted on its front face: a square frame whose square opening faces the robot and is closed at the back by a red plate. Insert the peg: the centre of the peg's front end (the end pointing ahead at the start) must be inside the square opening and more than 2 cm deep into it (the opening is 3 cm deep up to the red plate).
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. Its distance, its sideways offset and its tilt (the top leaning toward or away from the robot by up to 30 degrees) vary between instances. On the wall's front face sits an immovable socket: a blue plastic square frame 4 cm thick, mounted flat on the wall, around a square opening perpendicular to the wall face; a red plate (1 cm thick, flush with the wall) closes the opening 3 cm behind the frame's front face. Nominally the frame's outer side is 10 cm and the opening 6 cm; both are scaled by one factor between 0.75 and 1.5 (opening 4.5 to 9 cm square), the depth unchanged. Where the socket sits on the central part of the wall varies between instances. The iron-coloured peg is a free rigid body (it falls if let go); at every reset it is placed between the gripper's fingers, centred at the gripper's tool point with its axis along the tool's forward axis, and the gripper is commanded closed, so the robot starts holding it. Nothing else moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed on the peg.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl (loaded from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server). At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the centre becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently, and the orientation becomes quat_from_euler_xyz(0, pitch, 0) with pitch ~ U(-pi/6, pi/6) rad (a rotation about the world y axis through the wall centre; positive pitch tilts the top of the wall away from the robot, the front normal turning upward). Socket: kinematic rigid body hole.usd (gravity disabled). At each reset, after the wall, its root is placed at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.07, hy, hz) with hy, hz ~ U(-0.3, 0.3) m independently and given the wall's orientation, so its local +x is the wall normal pointing into the wall and the root (the socket's centre) is 0.02 m in front of the wall surface; AM-Bench's goal_pos observation is this root position. Local geometry before scaling: four boxes 0.04 m deep (x from -0.02 to 0.02) forming a square frame of outer side 0.10 m around the opening |y|, |z| < 0.03 m; a red box GoalRegion 0.01 x 0.06 x 0.06 m with collision at x from 0.01 to 0.02 closing the opening; frame material Polycarbonate_Opaque.mdl 'Polycarbonate_Blue' (from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server); physics material static friction 0.8, dynamic 0.6, restitution 0. Scale (1, s, s) (local y and z only) with s ~ U(0.75, 1.5), drawn once when the environment is created (a prestartup event), not at each reset. Peg: rigid body peg.usd, cylinder along its local x, length 0.15 m, radius 0.02 m, root at its centre, mass 0.01 kg, gravity on, physics material static friction 2.0, dynamic 1.5, restitution 0, visual material Iron.mdl (from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server). At each reset, after the robot, the peg is placed at the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + R(ee_link) (0.18, 0, 0)) with the ee_link orientation and zero velocity: centre at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m, axis along world x, tip (+0.075 m along its local x) at about (0.482, 0, 1.124) m. The gripper target is set to closed (-1, the finger joints' lower limit 0.001 m); the FA-Hexa defines no object-width converter, so the finger joints are not preset to the peg's 0.04 m diameter. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success at a control step when the peg tip p = peg root position + R(peg) (0.075, 0, 0) (the centre of the end face that points ahead at reset), expressed in the socket's frame as q = R(socket)^T (p - socket root position), satisfies q.x > 0 (peg_insertion_depth_min = 0: past the socket's mid-plane, i.e. more than 0.02 m behind its front face; the red plate's surface is at q.x = 0.01), |q.y| < 0.03 s and |q.z| < 0.03 s (half the scaled opening side 0.06 s); all inequalities strict. Only this point is tested: the peg's orientation, whether it is still held and contacts are not checked. AM-Bench reports no subtask criteria for this task. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
difficulty_note: The opening can be as small as 4.5 cm square for the 4 cm peg, the wall tilt of up to 30 degrees changes the insertion direction per instance along with the socket's place, and the peg is held only by the gripper's grip on a free-flying, hovering base.
standard_notes: The socket's pose, the wall's tilt and the opening's size are not given, nor is the peg's pose (it can shift in the grip): the blue socket on the concrete wall has to be found with the onboard cameras (the held peg occupies part of the end-effector camera's view) and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses). Insertion depth can only be judged visually.
